 Titus Welliver will reprise his role as Harry Bosch through audiobook narration for Michael Connelly's upcoming novel The Hollow , scheduled for release in the United States on October 27, 2026. Welliver will share narration duties with Cameron Monaghan, who is also set to portray a younger version of the detective in MGM+'s prequel series Bosch: Start of Watch. The novel revisits a formative case from Bosch's childhood, connecting the veteran detective's personal history to an unresolved death at a children's facility.
 According to Collider, the story centers on the murder of Bosch's mother when he was 11 and his subsequent placement at MacLaren Children's Center, where abuse was widespread. Decades after the facility closed, a class action lawsuit resulted in a multibillion-dollar settlement for former residents. Bosch's half-brother, defense attorney Mickey Haller, informs him that he is entitled to $400,000, but the detective declines the money and instead pursues answers about a former fellow resident's death.

 The boy, known as Chops, was found dead in a concealed space beneath a staircase used by staff to discipline children. The death was covered up and remained unsolved, prompting Bosch to reopen the investigation despite the possibility that the person responsible may already be dead.

 Welliver portrayed Bosch throughout seven seasons of Bosch and continued in the role for three seasons of Bosch: Legacy, which ended in 2025. The character's television universe has since expanded through Ballard on Prime Video, while The Hollow offers another opportunity for Welliver to return to the detective without extending the retired character's television storyline. The Hollow will be available in print, ebook and audiobook formats in the United States on October 27. Its UK hardcover edition is scheduled for November 5, according to Collider's October 20 report.
 Welliver's upcoming audiobook work comes as another crime thriller featuring the actor continues to attract streaming attention. The Town, directed by and starring Ben Affleck, features Welliver alongside Rebecca Hall, Blake Lively, Jeremy Renner and Jon Hamm. Released theatrically in 2010, The Town follows bank robber Doug MacRay, who develops feelings for Claire Keesey, a bank employee taken hostage during a robbery. The relationship complicates his plans to leave criminal life behind, placing both his personal future and his associates at risk.
 According to Collider's October 11 and October 17 reports, The Town was produced on a reported budget of $37 million and earned more than $154 million worldwide. The film received a 92% critics' score and an 85% audience score on Rotten Tomatoes, while Renner earned an Academy Award nomination for his performance. The film is scheduled to remain available on HBO Max in the United States until November 1, 2026. Affleck also collaborated with Welliver on Gone Baby Gone, Live By Night and Argo, extending their professional partnership beyond The Town.
